data.name: Pansy
data.gender_notes: Pansy is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word pan (all) and sos (I work), Pansy is a name that means 'all flowers' or 'all beauty'. In ancient Greece, the name was given to a goddess of nature and fertility. In Christianity, it may be associated with the Pan of the Bible, a shepherd figure who represents God's care and protection. The name Pansy carries the meaning “Flower, Beauty” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Pansy usually hope their child will grow to embody flower, beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of God's care and protection, beauty, and nature.
data.etymology: Pansy belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Flower, Beauty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pansy total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: פנסי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פנסי מקורו ביוונית ופירושו פרח סגול, יופי, שמחה. הוא משויך לצמח הפנסיה, שגם הוא נקרא כך בשל צבעו הסגול. השם משקף את היופי והשמחה שבפרח ומשמש כסמל לאושר ולשמחה.

in_greek.name: Πάνσυ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Πάνσυ προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη για το λουλούδι πανσέρι, το οποίο ονομάστηκε έτσι λόγω του μοβ χρώματός του. Το όνομα αντανακλά την ομορφιά και τη χαρά που συνδέονται με το λουλούδι και χρησιμοποιείται ως σύμβολο ευτυχίας και χαράς.

in_latin.name: Pansy
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Pansy is derived from the Latin word for the purple flower, viola. It reflects the beauty and joy associated with the flower and serves as a symbol of happiness and delight. The name has been used in Christian tradition to signify modesty and humility.

in_english.name: Pansy
in_english.meaning: A flower name symbolizing love, loyalty, and devotion
in_english.long_meaning: The name Pansy originates from the Greek word for the purple flower, viola. It was adopted into Latin as viola and later into English as Pansy. In Christian tradition, the name Pansy symbolizes love, loyalty, and devotion. It is often associated with the virtues of modesty and humility. The name has been used since the 16th century and has been popularized in literature and poetry.

data.cultural_impact: The name Pansy has a rich history in various cultures. In ancient Greece, Pansy was the name of a goddess of nature, fertility, and wild places. The name may have also been associated with the god Pan, a shepherd deity. In medieval Europe, the name Pansy became popular due to the pansy flower, which was believed to symbolize thoughts and memories. In modern times, the term "pansy," although pejorative, has been reclaimed by the LGBTQ+ community to mean someone who is effeminate or feminine, particularly in a homosexual or bisexual man.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Pansy holds various spiritual significances. One interpretation is that it is a reminder of God's all-encompassing love and care for his creation. As a name for a goddess of nature, it may also represent the beauty and wonder of God's world and the importance of appreciating nature as part of our spiritual lives. Furthermore, the name's association with the shepherd figure Pan may symbolize God's protection and care for his people, as a shepherd watches over and cares for his flock.
